title: Last-coordinate duplication identity
statement: Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $F$ be a real-valued family indexed by $F_2^{k+1}$ with values that are functions on $F_2^n$, let $b\in\mathbb F_2$, and let $s\in F_2^{k+1}$. If the last-coordinate duplication of $F$ at $b$ is evaluated at $s$, the result is $F$ evaluated at the point whose first $k$ coordinates are those of $s$ and whose last coordinate is $b$.
hypotheses_covered: $F$ is a real-valued family on the indicated cubes
